claim.why_it_matters: Plain paragraph rather than a heading, while its siblings '#### 4.2.2.1.1 User-Defined Words' (page 152) and '#### 4.2.2.1.4 Function-Names' (page 155) are headings; the outline loses clause IV.4.2.2.1.2.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page 154 (folio IV-8) sets '4.2.2.1.2 System-Names' as a numbered clause heading on its own line, the same style as '4.2.2.1.3 Reserved Words' and '4.2.2.1.3.1 Required Words' below it. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md line 6513 it is a bare paragraph '4.2.2.1.2 System-Names' with no '####' marker, while siblings 4.2.2.1.1 (line 6429), 4.2.2.1.1.1-5, 4.2.2.1.3.2 (6561) and 4.2.2.1.4 (6587) are '####' headings. The text is present; only its structure is lost, so the claim is accurate as a structural (outline) defect, not a content-wording one. The same defect also affects '4.2.2.1.3 Reserved Words' (line 6525) and '4.2.2.1.3.1 Required Words' (line 6545) on this same page.
verdict.corrected_description: Accurate. Additionally, on the same page '4.2.2.1.3 Reserved Words' and '4.2.2.1.3.1 Required Words' are likewise plain paragraphs rather than '####' headings, so the outline loses three clauses on page 154 (IV.4.2.2.1.2, IV.4.2.2.1.3, IV.4.2.2.1.3.1), unless separate claims cover them.
